name: KERF

intro.problem: KERF combines a maximum-entropy synthetic background [@jaynes1957] with kernel-based models of its marginals and of the dependence between them, because ABCD estimates that assume the two discriminants factorize fail when the discriminants are correlated, most of all in sparse tails [@choi2021].
intro.value: A background model that keeps the fitted marginals but learns their dependence, rather than removing it during training [@abcdisco2021][@cms2025tec], turns non-closure from a failure into a measured and correctable quantity.
intro.approach: The first model built a maximum-entropy background from fitted per-feature marginals with hand-picked copula dependence. KERF keeps those marginals and replaces the copula with an exponential tilt whose functions are chosen from the data by kernel maximal correlation [@renyi1959][@huang2020], extending to a full kernel exponential family [@sriperumbudur2017], with every variant scored on closure through a gated test plan.
intro.goals: The end goal is an improved, and potentially novel, data-driven background estimate: a kernel maximum-entropy model whose dependence term comes with honest uncertainties and is benchmarked against extended and Bayesian ABCD methods [@choi2021][@alvarez2024].

questions: Can a kernel-chosen dependence term recover the correlation that a factorized estimate misses?
Does it improve on the hand-picked copulas of the first maximum-entropy model, especially in the sparse tail where the signal region sits?
Can a flexible background model stay honest: closing on held-out regions without absorbing injected signal?

timeline.label: MaxEnt background model specified: product of fitted marginals plus dependence rungs
First MaxEnt ladder run: product baseline, Gaussian copula, and mixture copula rungs
Second-generation MaxEnt planned; literature and novelty check
Kernel MaxEnt plan locked: kernel-selected dependence term, gated test plan, genealogy deck
Kernel models explored for the low-statistics barrel region
Formalized as its own project and named KERF
Gated tests: toy harness, structure check, blinded toy closure, held-out corners, signal injection

links.title: Applied in the barrel program
links.text: The barrel is the region where a factorized estimate is least trustworthy and statistics are thinnest. STAVE applies this joint-background model there and scores it against the shared barrel baseline.

tagline: Maximum-entropy synthetic background with kernel-modeled marginals and dependence

components.name: MaxEnt synthetic background
components.subtitle: The first model
components.summary: Per-feature marginals fitted to the total background, sampled as a product (plain ABCD), then with Gaussian and mixture copulas added as dependence rungs [@jaynes1957].

components.name: Kernel dependence
components.subtitle: Let the data choose the constraint
components.summary: Keep the marginals fixed and model the linking term as an exponential tilt. Kernel maximal correlation picks the functions [@renyi1959][@huang2020]; distance correlation is itself a kernel statistic, which ties this to the decorrelation line [@sejdinovic2013]. A density-ratio critic is an alternative route to the same term [@vandenoord2018].

items.label: Tilt
items.detail: One kernel-chosen pair of functions; plain ABCD is the case where the tilt is zero

items.label: Full family
items.detail: A kernel exponential family with the truncation removed, only if the tilt leaves structure behind [@sriperumbudur2017]

items.label: Tail bases
items.detail: Kernels that revert to factorization in the corner are avoided where the signal region sits

components.name: Gated tests
components.subtitle: Earn each step before the next
components.summary: Toy harness, structure diagnosis, blinded toy closure, held-out pseudo-signal regions on real background, then signal injection to check the model does not absorb signal.
